summary: Restored 100-foot steel fire tower in Palisades Park, Blount County; watched for forest fires 1949-1985, reopened to free climbs after a 2016-2018 restoration.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a cab reached by 133 steps

access.note: Climbing is free; a 2026 event listing says so, and a 2018 guide advised getting a free permit from the park office.

visit.trail_note: 133 steps up to the cab inside Palisades Park

events.note: Cab used by workers watching for forest fires and wildfires in Blount County from 1949, per a 2018 news report
Cab use by fire watchers ends in 1985, per a 2018 news report; the report gives no build date
Registered May 27, 2016 as US 1130, AL 63; restoration work began in 2016
Restoration finished early 2018; the tower was opened to climbers as the second restored Alabama tower open to the public

evidence.supports: 100-foot steel tower that formerly belonged to the Alabama Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: This 100-foot steel tower formerly belonged to the Alabama Forestry Commission.

evidence.supports: now part of Palisades Park and restored
evidence.quote: Now part of Palisades Park, it has been restored.

evidence.supports: cab used by workers watching for forest fires from 1949 to 1985
evidence.quote: The cab that sits over 100 feet off the ground is the same one used by workers who watched for forest fires and wildfires in Blount County from 1949-1985.

evidence.supports: having a person in the cab was no longer necessary, so the tower sat empty
evidence.quote: When technology advanced and population increased, having a person inside the cab was not necessary. As a result, the tower sat empty.

evidence.supports: county saw the tower as a landmark to preserve
evidence.quote: Blount County saw the tower as a landmark
Back in 2016, restoration work began, and with help from several grants, local businesses, and other people, the work was finished in early 2018.

evidence.supports: third fire tower restored in the state and second opened to the public
evidence.quote: the tower is the third fire tower restored in the state and second opened to the public, park officials said.

evidence.supports: climb the 133 steps inside Palisades Park
evidence.quote: When you climb the 133 steps of the Sand Mountain Lookout Fire Tower inside Palisades Park

evidence.supports: Alabama Forestry Commission can still use the tower, including in a large forest fire
evidence.quote: Bullard said the Alabama Forestry Commission is able to use the tower anytime needed as well as in the event of a large forest fire.

evidence.supports: the restored tower is the park's newest feature
evidence.quote: The newest feature is the restored Fire Tower.

evidence.supports: visitors should get a free permit from the park office to climb
evidence.quote: Visit the park office for a free permit to climb the tower.
Park information current as of July 31, 2018

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the tower formerly belonged to the Alabama Forestry Commission and is now part of Palisades Park, which administers it; the 2018 news report says the commission can still use it when needed.

sources.title: Blount County hopes to take tourism to new heights

notes_for_editor: Construction year unknown: neither the Register nor the 2018 news report gives it. A Blount County museum Facebook post seen only as a search snippet says built 1949 and staffed to about 1972, then sporadically to 1985; it could not be read, so it is not used. Height: the record's height_m 33.0 does not match the Register's '100-foot steel tower' (30.5 m), though the 2018 report says the cab sits over 100 feet up, so the record may count a different height. Not corrected. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the 2018 report saying the tower sat empty; current staffing is not confirmed. A separate Facebook snippet about a 1931 tower on Green Knob Mountain is a different tower and was not used. Access is from a 2026 event listing and a 2018 guide, so check the park before a visit.
